cards.body:
## Summary
Make `table-core` the only author of what makes a mandate unsignable: a closed `MandateProblem` enum, a `MandatePayload::problems()` that returns every problem, and a generated `bindings/mandateProblems.ts` table the client keys its plain words by, instead of three hand copies matched on English text.

## Description
Today `validate()` (mandate.rs:262) is written once in Rust with free-text reasons and copied twice in TypeScript: `ruleProblems` (mandateDraft.ts:275) for the live editor and `mockValidate` (mock/simulate.ts:61) for the browser mock. A fourth partial copy sits in lib/marketWatch.ts. The client turns Rust's REFUSED text into words through `REFUSAL_WORDS`, keyed by the exact English reason (mandateDraft.ts:351). The copies have already drifted: the mock has no lever (clause 8) checks, no rescue/subscribers pairing, and leaves the lever discount out of the currency check, so the judge path (mock) signs rescue mandates Rust refuses. Any rewording of a Rust reason silently drops the client to its generic fallback, and nothing fails.

The move: each `return Err(Refusal::new(n, "..."))` in validate becomes a `MandateProblem` variant with `clause()` and `reason()` (the reason text kept byte-identical). `problems()` collects them in today's order; `validate()` is `problems().first()` turned into a `Refusal`, so the wire and every agent refusal code stay the same. `table-client` emits `MandateProblem.ts` and `mandateProblems.ts` (code -> clause, reason) next to `ladder.ts`, freshness-checked by the existing bindings test. The client's word table becomes `Record<MandateProblem, string>` (a new Rust variant is a tsc error), `refusalWords` resolves text -> code through the generated table, and `mockValidate` returns codes with the missing lever and rescue checks added, pinned by tests.

## Flow
- Rust: MandateProblem enum + problems(); validate() delegates; golden test of the 23 reason texts.
- table-client: mandate_problems::typescript(), generate-bindings writes it, tests/bindings.rs checks it and visits MandateProblem.
- Client: REFUSAL_WORDS keyed by code; refusalWords via MANDATE_PROBLEMS; ruleProblems reuses the same word table where its rule matches a code.
- Mock: mockValidate returns codes, gains lever + rescue + lever-currency checks.

## Expected impact
One place to change a signing rule; a wording change or new rule cannot reach the owner as the generic 'they don’t fit' sentence; the mock (the no-install judge path) stops signing mandates the wallet refuses. It also gives the post-submission T13 clause tree a typed per-clause problem vocabulary to build on.

## Evaluation
Claim: the three validation copies collapse onto one Rust problem list, and the mock's drift is closed.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no problems(), no generated table, mock returns null for the three lever/rescue cases).
After: 7 of 7 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked validate() 263-466 into an ordered variant list; walked mockValidate 61-104 against the lever/rescue/currency inputs; the gate rung is the builder's
Result: better
Gate: contract (in-repo generated bindings only; the Refusal wire form and text are unchanged; nothing consumed outside the repo).

cards.title: Derive the deal-state sets from transition() and generate them for the client
shared_surfaces: bindings/ directory (generate-bindings clean-set + orphan check; same files as slot A - if both cards are built, serialize them)
acceptance: for every s in DealState::ALL -> DealState::withdrawable(s) == transition(s, DealEvent::Withdraw).is_ok(); AUTHORIZED is not withdrawable, APPROVED is

mock fair price: fairPriceOf('EXPIRED', certifiedMarket, price).committed -> true (an EXPIRED deal went through AGREED; the mock's AGREED_OR_LATER at fairPrice.ts:53-55 omits EXPIRED today and returns false)

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/gating.ts:59-62 - '/** Rust `transition(s, Withdraw)` ... */ export const WITHDRAWABLE' hand copy

apps/desktop/client/src/mock/forecast.ts:107 - a second set in the same file, ENDED, documented as '`DealState::terminal()` in table-core'

cards.body:
## Summary
Derive the deal-state classifications (withdrawable, released, agreed-or-later) from `transition()` itself, keep each as one list in `table-core`, and generate them into `bindings/dealStates.ts` so the approval window and the mock import them instead of keeping five hand copies.

## Description
`DealState` has 21 states and four hand-written predicates (pre_capture, terminal, is_released, is_agreed_or_later); `RELEASED` is written twice in the same file (deal.rs:140-152), and the withdraw rule `pre_capture && != Authorized` is spelled out three times inside `transition()`. The client copies these sets five more times (gating.ts TERMINAL/WITHDRAWABLE, fairPrice.ts, mock/exposure.ts, mock/forecast.ts twice), and two copies already disagree with Rust: the mock forecast forecasts MISMATCH deals Rust skips, and the mock fair price calls an EXPIRED deal uncommitted while MISMATCH (reachable from LISTED) counts as committed. Every new state (UNCONFIRMED was the last, DECISIONS §28) has to be added to 9 lists by hand.

The move: add `withdrawable()` and a test-time reachability walk over `transition()` that pins `is_agreed_or_later` and `RELEASED` to the graph; emit a `DEAL_STATES` value (`terminal`, `pre_capture`, `released`, `agreed_or_later`, `withdrawable`, each a `ReadonlySet<DealState>`) through `table-client` exactly like `ladder.ts`; replace the client copies with imports. forecast.ts's local TERMINAL becomes the Rust terminal set plus its own explicit 'nothing left to schedule' states, so the difference is named, not accidental.

## Flow
- table-core: withdrawable(); transition's Withdraw/Mismatch/Fail arms call it; graph-derived tests.
- table-client: deal_states::typescript(); generate-bindings + bindings test.
- Client: gating.ts, fairPrice.ts, mock/exposure.ts, mock/forecast.ts import @bindings/dealStates.

## Expected impact
A state added or reclassified in Rust reaches every window and the mock in one regenerate, and a stale copy fails CI. Fixes two live mock drifts on the judge path.

## Evaluation
Claim: the deal-state sets have one source, derived from the transition table, and the client cannot drift from it.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (no withdrawable(), no graph test, no generated file; mock forecast emits a MISMATCH line; fairPriceOf('EXPIRED').committed is false).
After: 6 of 6 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked transition() (deal.rs:264-299) by hand for reachability-through-AGREED: {AGREED, SETTLING, AWAITING_APPROVAL, APPROVED, AUTHORIZED, CAPTURED, RECEIPTED, RECONCILED, UNCONFIRMED, REFUNDED, DISPUTED, VOIDED, AUTO_VOIDED, EXPIRED}; minus released {VOIDED, AUTO_VOIDED, EXPIRED} equals is_agreed_or_later's 11; the gate rung is the builder's
Result: better
Gate: none (no wire, ledger or IPC change; generated in-repo constant only).

never_repropose_checked: Ruled out T12 mandate what-if (built; card A touches validate() not simulate/check replay), T11 authority manifest (built; covers commands/capabilities, not domain sets or refusal reasons), T14 exposure (built; card B only re-sources its mock's state sets), T13 clause tree (post-submission, not adopted), DECISIONS §5 (band fails closed - kept, its 'client mirror' is what card A collapses) and §39 (exact-text sentence matching precedent - card A removes that pattern for mandate refusals).
